summary: All 14 selected behavioral test entrypoints pass. Two separate restricted Orca launches produced concrete startup failures. Copied existing Grok credentials reached current idle UI, replacing the prior login-blocker assumption; its different footer is unknown on untouched base and target. Weekly-limit choice was not forced because zero spend could not be guaranteed. No source fix is warranted by the observed results.

scenarios.name: Orca exit and relaunch preserves files and reuses or replaces terminal
scenarios.error: runtime_serve_failed: Orca serve aborted with SIGABRT on macOS.
scenarios.cause: The write-restricted named lab could not start packaged Electron Orca. The policy allows file writes only inside this worktree (plus /dev/null), and denies Mach service lookup to prevent writes mediated by external services. The runtime itself reported startup-registration failure. This is a limitation of the restricted launch tested, not proof that every possible Orca isolation method is unavailable. No shared-runtime terminal was created.

fixture_substitution.result: pass; disconnected replacement keeps the recorded worktree, connected dead terminal reuse keeps its handle; closed endpoint exit sends nothing. These are fixture proofs, not a live proof of local-file preservation.

scenarios.name: Orca relaunch refuses surviving agent or unreadable endpoint without duplicate launch
scenarios.error: runtime_serve_failed: Orca serve aborted with SIGABRT on macOS.
scenarios.cause: A separately named, write-restricted duplicate-refusal lab failed before a runtime endpoint existed. No fleet endpoint was used and no mutation command was sent to the shared running app.

fixture_substitution.result: pass; live-agent, agent-in-worktree, unreadable, ambiguous and failed scan all refuse before terminal creation and retain existing task metadata. Real stand-in process cases ran without skips.

scenarios.name: Grok idle bordered composer with adjacent hint row reads empty
scenarios.result: live attempted; required historical layout unavailable
scenarios.observed: Using a COPY of the existing supported auth file reached Grok Build 1.0.70 idle. Its actual footer is Weekly limit left: 0% · Grok 4.7 (high), with no adjacent key-hint row. It displays the default-off training banner; neither option was selected. The classifier returns unknown for this shape on BOTH untouched base and target, so this is not a regression introduced by the carry-over. This does not establish empty recognition for the requested 1.0.62 layout.

fixture_substitution.result: pass; recorded 1.0.62 middle-dot title and adjacent hint classify empty when idle and pending when typed through production classifier and Orca adapter.

scenarios.name: Grok weekly-limit choice is a blocking dialog without purchase
scenarios.observed: Authenticated startup shows Weekly limit left: 0% but no weekly-limit choice. Production dialog detection returns exit 1 on the actual capture on base and target. A cached 0% label does not guarantee a new submitted request cannot consume credits. No request was submitted, no training/privacy preference selected, no authentication approval sent, no quota consumed intentionally and no purchase confirmed. Triggering a server-side rejection to force the choice was not attempted under the zero-spend/account-state constraint.

fixture_substitution.result: pass; exact recorded dialog is named Grok weekly-limit choice and cannot read empty; missing-choice and quoted-transcript variants do not match.

verification_scope: Only selected existing test functions, two restricted Orca launch probes, and a prompt-free real Grok startup. No full suite, linter, formatter, static analysis, pipeline command, push, PR or CI action.

cleanup.note: Copied auth file, generated Grok data, private terminal socket, sandbox policies, fixture roots and generated runners removed. No prepare dependencies removed.
